text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT PAGE — seg-cache degradation observed in us-west-2. Paging on-call: @ashok.oncall. Severity: P2. Impact: elevated errors for streaming generation and higher tail latency for some customers. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/r/seg-cache-degrade

emily.sre: saw a sudden drop in seg-cache hit-rate at 18:00 UTC, CPU on inference nodes spiking ~60% above baseline. traces show repeated cache misses for the same namespace keys.

dan.runtime: looks like a malformed client pattern is causing many unique namespace prefixes; traffic entropy jumped x30. I can throttle at the edge for the offending tenant if we want quick relief.

maya.product: which customers are affected? any enterprise tenants on Dedicated?

emily.sre: primarily two hostnames in logs: acme-corp.prod and skylinesearch.prod — both on hosted. Error rates for acme-corp have gone from 0.1% -> 6% for generation endpoints.

ashok.oncall: taking pager. quick plan: 1) apply per-tenant ingress rate limit for acme-corp to ~200rps 2) temporarily disable seg-cache for high-entropy namespaces to avoid cache thrash and correctness issues 3) enable short circuit bypass to backend model pool for those requests 4) watch latency and CPU.

dan.runtime: for step 2 I suggest a targeted bypass rather than global disable. We can add a routing rule: if namespace matches regex ^acme-.*(session|ctx).* then set header x-redwood-cache: bypass. Config snippet: ```json
{"matcher":"namespace","pattern":"^acme-.*(session|ctx).*$","action":"bypass-cache"}```

emily.sre: doing ingress qps cap now for acme-corp via rate-limiter service: `rlctl set acme-corp 200` — applying.

ops-runner-bot: rlctl: change queued, deploying to edge nodes. Expected propagation 20-30s.

ashok.oncall: rolling the bypass rule in 1min if rate cap doesn't drop error spikes. prepping rollback plan: remove rule and revert caps.

maya.product: pinged acme-corp CSM + support, told them we're applying a short cap and will follow up. No need to escalate to legal yet.

dan.runtime: added temporary traffic shaping in routing layer to smooth bursts: token-bucket with burst=100, refill=200/s for acme-corp. Command: `rtctl shape --tenant acme-corp --burst 100 --rate 200`

emily.sre: applied bypass rule for matched namespaces. Observing immediate decrease in backend error rate but CPU on some inference hosts rose slightly due to extra decode work (bypassing cache).

ashok.oncall: immediate mitigation check: errors down from 6% -> 1.2% for acme-corp, tail latency median +50ms. Good tradeoff. We'll keep bypass live for 45 minutes and monitor.

emily.sre: also lowered seg-cache eviction threshold to favor small keys (ttl bump for hot keys) to reduce churn: `cachectl set eviction_policy conservative && cachectl ttl-adjust --selector hot 60s` — this should help stabilize hit rate without reintroducing correctness problems.

dan.runtime: note: bypassing cache can surface model-fallbacks; watch for increased model fallbacks in the next 30m. Alerting on >2% fallback.

ops-runner-bot: alerting rule updated: model-fallback-rate(acme-corp) > 2% -> notify #eng-oncall and #runtime.

maya.product: will draft customer note: "We observed an unusual request pattern causing cache degradation; we've applied protective rate limits and a targeted cache bypass to restore correctness and reduce errors. We're monitoring and will provide timeline."

ashok.oncall: handing over to night on-call in 20m — @emily.sre will keep watch and escalate if thresholds breach. If error rate climbs >3% or latency >1s p95, rollback to prior config and open incident page.

emily.sre: ack. creating incident doc link with timeline: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1862500000/ — adding initial logs and mitigation steps.

dan.runtime: follow-ups: 1) permanent fix: add namespace entropy detection to routing and auto-apply per-tenant micro-throttles 2) add a safer cache bypass mode that avoids extra decode cost 3) evaluate client SDK changes to limit pathological patterns.

ops-runner-bot: rlctl: acme-corp rate cap update complete across 12 edge clusters.

ashok.oncall: closing active mitigation stage; keep monitoring for next 60m. If stable, we'll reopen and convert to postmortem for root cause + long-term fixes. :thumbsup:

emily.sre: last check at +14m: error rate 1.0%, seg-cache hit-rate recovering from 12% -> 45% for non-bypassed namespaces, CPU trending down.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — mitigations applied. Status: mitigated (P2). Next steps: postmortem + config hardening.

maya.product: thanks team, I'll coordinate customer follow-up and escalation if they ask for dedicated capacity.

ashok.oncall: handing off to night: @ashok.oncall -> @night-ops. keep the thread updated."
